b2b-marketers-who-cut-linkedin-ads-measu.author: Claire Dalton
b2b-marketers-who-cut-linkedin-ads-measu.core: Posted in last 7 days B2B Marketers Who Cut LinkedIn Ads - Measured Impact Over Time Have we become so accustomed to including LinkedIn in B2B media plans that we've stopped questioning whether it actually needs to be there? We're exploring a research report for 2027, and I'm looking to speak to B2B marketers who've deliberately removed or significantly reduced their LinkedIn advertising investment and measured the impact over a meaningful period of time. It's something I've been questioning, particularly following conversations with marketing teams across different sectors. I wonder whether the platform's targeting capabilities and perceived audience size have made it almost a default choice in B2B advertising. But just because thousands of profiles match our targeting criteria, how many of those people are actually active? And how differently do professional audiences use the platform? A campaign can deliver great results among the people it reaches while potentially missing a substantial proportion of its intended audience. And with budgets under increasing scrutiny, how often are we genuinely testing the incremental impact of our media investment, rather than relying on attributed results alone? I'm particularly interested in marketers who've challenged years of always-on investment. What happened when you reduced or removed it? Did pipeline suffer? Did demand continue elsewhere? Did the findings change future budget decisions, or reinforce the value of keeping LinkedIn in the mix? To be clear, this is about paid advertising, not LinkedIn's wider role in organic marketing, networking or sales. Nor is it about proving one channel is better than another. It's about questioning some of the assumptions behind our media investment decisions, particularly as audience behaviour continues to evolve. If you've tested this, I'd genuinely love to hear what you found, whatever the outcome!

former-treasury-officials-and-crypto-exe.core: Posted in last 7 days Former Treasury Officials & Crypto Execs - GENIUS Act Stablecoin Yield Banks Lose Stablecoin Yield Fight as OCC Final GENIUS Act Rule Keeps Crypto Rewards Alive The OCC's 721-page GENIUS Act rule went final on October 21, and banks did not get the limit on stablecoin rewards they asked for. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency kept one ban in place. Platforms such as Coinbase and Kraken can't pay you just for holding, using or keeping a stablecoin, Roll Call reported. Every other reward will be judged case by case. The draft rule had treated these deals as illegal unless the industry proved otherwise, and the final rule dropped that test. The two sides read it very differently: 1. American Bankers Association CEO Rob Nichols said the rule "will preserve the status quo for crypto platforms despite Congress's clear intent to protect local lending." 2. Blockchain Association chief policy officer Lindsay Fraser said, "We are especially grateful that the OCC listened to the industry." Banks care because they fund local loans with deposits, and they fear savers will move that money into stablecoins that pay rewards. The banks' next move is the Senate. The Clarity Act would let regulators stop yield payments if banks with under $10 billion in assets lose enough deposits to cause them serious harm. The rule takes effect on January 18, 2027. If an exchange paid you more on USDC than your bank pays on savings, would you move your savings out of the bank? I'd like to hear from Faryar Shirzad, Rebeca Romero Rainey, Simon Taylor and Austin Campbell. #Stablecoins #GENIUSAct #Fintech #Banking Roll Call

deaf-people-in-uk-organisation-failures-.author: Helen T.
deaf-people-in-uk-organisation-failures-.core: Posted in last 7 days Deaf People in UK - Organisation Failures Affecting Health & Rights HOW MANY TIMES CAN AN ORGANISATION FAIL A DEAF PERSON BEFORE SOMEONE FINALLY HOLDS THEM ACCOUNTABLE? I want to ask Deaf people across the UK something important. What is the most shocking experience you've had with an organisation because you're Deaf? Not just an inconvenience. I mean experiences that have genuinely affected your health, safety, finances, employment, independence, dignity or basic human rights. Perhaps a bank made it impossible to access your own money because you couldn't use the telephone. A hospital failed to provide a BSL interpreter when you desperately needed to understand what was happening to your health. A government department, local council or public service repeatedly ignored your communication requirements. An employer denied you opportunities or refused reasonable adjustments. Or perhaps an airline, insurer, police force, university, housing provider or another organisation left you facing a barrier hearing people would never even have to consider. But here's what I REALLY want to know. WHAT HAPPENED WHEN YOU TRIED TO PUT IT RIGHT? Did you complain and get nowhere? Were you passed from department to department? Were you told there was no budget, no interpreter, no alternative or simply that it was company policy? Did someone apologise, promise improvements and then do absolutely nothing? Did you have to fight for months or even years? Or did you eventually give up because the process of challenging discrimination became another barrier itself? I especially want to hear about experiences that remain unresolved. And yes, I want to know the names of the organisations involved. Not just "a bank" or "a hospital". WHICH bank? WHICH NHS Trust? WHICH council? WHICH employer? WHICH company? Tell me: 1. WHO was the organisation? 2. WHAT happened, and how seriously did it affect you? 3. HOW did they respond when you challenged them? 4. IS IT STILL HAPPENING, despite your attempts to resolve it? If you have written complaints or evidence, please mention that too. You can comment or message me privately, including in BSL. Please avoid sharing sensitive personal information or naming individual staff publicly. I won't publish your personal account without your permission. I keep wondering how many Deaf people are fighting exactly the same battles against exactly the same organisations, unaware of each other. How many complaints have been closed without anything actually changing? How many organisations believe they're accessible simply because they have an accessibility policy? And how many Deaf people have stopped complaining, not because the problem was resolved, but because they were exhausted from fighting? That's what I want to understand. Please share this widely. I particularly want to hear from Deaf people whose experiences have never been taken seriously. Because a complaint being closed does not mean the discrimination has stopped. #DeafRights #BSL #Accessibility #DeafCommunity #DisabilityRights

women-changing-direction-raw-midpivot-st.core: Posted in last 7 days Women Changing Direction - Raw Mid-Pivot Stories I am looking for guests for the WIP’n & Reppin’podcast! If you have changed direction, or you’re deep in the middle of changing it right now, and it’s nowhere near tidy - I would love to hear your story. You do not need to be perfectly polished or have completed 10 pivots smoothly like an olympic acrobat! I want to speak to women who have had the courage to take the leap and are willing the share the real, uncertain middle nobody puts in the highlight reel - because that stuff is THE GOLD right there, the real stuff others often won't share. That is the stuff that helps others through tough times, helps someone decide whether they keep going or not, and potentially saves someone from an avoidable costly mistake. Maybe you have left a career that looked good on paper, started something that scared you, moved countries, changed everything in your thirties or forties — or maybe you're living in that middle stage right now, and not sure what is on the other side yet... You don’t need a big following or a perfect ending - that's not the spirit of WIP'n & Reppin' - we know things take time to navigate, cultivate, and build. You just need a real story - and the willingness to tell it straight - that can inspire and educate other women in similar stages who might not know which way to turn right now. If you know someone perfect for this - maybe even yourself? (You are allowed to be proud and share your own story!) OK, now send me all the amazingly brave audacious women you know making moves, please - I can't wait to hear all the stories! #podcastguests #shareyourstory #careerpivot WIP'n & Reppin'

women-in-south-west-nigeria-shrinking-ci.headline: Women in South West Nigeria - Shrinking Civic Space Testimonies
women-in-south-west-nigeria-shrinking-ci.author: Vision Spring Initiatives V.S.I
women-in-south-west-nigeria-shrinking-ci.core: Posted in last 7 days Women in South West Nigeria - Shrinking Civic Space Testimonies YOUR STORY MATTERS. YOUR VOICE DESERVES TO BE HEARD. What happens when women speak up, organise, lead, report, teach or challenge the status quo? Too often, they face intimidation, sexualised harassment, reputational attacks, economic exclusion and digital surveillance simply for making their voices heard. But these experiences should not remain hidden, undocumented or unheard. Through Women Reclaiming Voice, a 2026 project by Vision Spring Initiatives (VSI) in partnership with Spaces for Change, we invite women across South West Nigeria to share their lived experiences of shrinking civic space. Whether you work in civil society, media, education, the informal economy, creative industries or digital spaces, we want to hear your story. Your experience matters. Whether you have been silenced, intimidated, excluded or threatened, or have found ways to resist, organise and keep going, your story deserves to be documented. You can share your experience through a short video, voice note, written narrative or social media thread. You may remain anonymous, request voice distortion or choose to be identified. Your safety and consent remain central to this process. Selected stories will contribute to The Living Archive, a collection documenting women's experiences of civic space from 2020 to date. They may also be adapted into videos, audio features, quote cards and story slides, amplifying women's voices through VSI's Feminist Hub and social media. 📅 Submission period: 12 October – 11 November 2026 🌍 Languages: English, Yoruba or Pidgin 📩 Email: [email redacted] 📱 Social media: @vsi_ng Your story is evidence. Your voice can strengthen solidarity, support accountability and contribute to the changes women deserve. It can also remind another woman that she is not alone. You do not have to be silent about what you have experienced. Help us document the realities of shrinking civic space and reclaim the voices that have been pushed aside. In solidarity, Vision Spring Initiatives (VSI) #womenreclaimingvoice #shrinkingcivicspace

There are no right or wrong answers — I want to hear about your experiences and perspectives. If you currently work in a school support role, or have done so recently, I’d be grateful if you’d consider speaking with me for my report. Please feel free to comment below or send me a private message if you’d be happy to have a conversation.
